VeraGridEngine.Templates.BasicBlockCatalog.lookup_array_runtime_templates.build_lookup_array_linear_variable_runtime_template(vf: VarFactory, point_count: int, clip: bool, name: str | None = None) → EmtModelTemplate[source]

Build a linear lookup whose complete table is supplied by signals.

The first port is the lookup coordinate, followed by every x breakpoint and then every y sample. A stable positional naming scheme allows General Options to increase or decrease the point count while retaining surviving diagram connections.

Parameters:

  • vf – Variable factory used to allocate symbolic objects.

  • point_count – Number of dynamic table points; at least two are required.

  • clip – Whether values outside the table are clipped or extrapolated.

  • name – Optional explicit runtime template name.

Returns:

Materialized EMT template with signal-driven table coordinates.

Raises:

ValueError – If fewer than two points are requested.

Wrap a configurable minimum or maximum block in the builder contract.

Builder-backed Library entries return model templates so creation, preflight validation, and structural editing all consume the same type. The inner block remains an ordinary symbolic block and retains the configurable input_count structure.

Parameters:

  • var_factory – Variable factory receiving the generated variables.

  • input_count – Number of signals participating in the reduction.

  • block_type – BlockType.MIN or BlockType.MAX.

Returns:

EMT template containing the requested extremum block.

VeraGridEngine.Templates.BasicBlockCatalog.predefined_blocks.extremum(var_factory: VarFactory, input_count: int, block_type: BlockType) → Block[source]

Build a minimum or maximum reduction over a configurable number of inputs.

The operation is represented by ordinary binary symbolic function nodes. Folding those nodes keeps the model proportional to the number of inputs instead of expanding every comparison into repeated Heaviside expressions.

Parameters:

  • var_factory – Variable factory receiving the generated block variables.

  • input_count – Number of input signals participating in the reduction.

  • block_type – BlockType.MIN or BlockType.MAX.

Returns:

Structural minimum or maximum block.

Raises:

ValueError – If fewer than two inputs or an unsupported block type is requested.
